D013-D020_h001.question:
It’s been going on… I’d say around five months now. I get choked up over the smallest things. Sometimes I’ll just start crying in the supply closet at work and I can’t even say exactly why. My wife asks what’s wrong and I can’t give her a straight answer; I just feel like I’m about to burst into tears all the time.

I move slower now. Walking the halls, pushing the cart, even bending down to pick up a mop bucket feels like I’m wading through mud. The other guys joke that I’m “getting old,” but it’s more than that—I just can’t seem to get myself going like before.

What really eats at me is this feeling that everything bad that happens is somehow my fault. If a tenant slips, or someone in the building gets sick, I catch myself thinking, “If I’d done more, maybe that wouldn’t have happened.” I know it doesn’t quite make sense, but I can’t shake it.

Most nights I lie there thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning anything, but the thought of not having to deal with any of this anymore crosses my mind a lot, especially with the pressure at work and money being tighter lately. It’s making it hard to keep up with my job and with things at home.
D013-D020_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h001.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

Sometimes, when I’m crossing the street or standing on the subway platform, there’s this sudden urge to just step out, or if I’m on a balcony, a pull to jump. I haven’t made any plans, but those thoughts scare me. It’s getting harder to keep up with deadlines and basic stuff like cooking or showering.

D013-D020_h023.question:
I guess the simplest way to put it is that I’ve just felt… low, kind of flat and sad, for what must be over a year now. It’s not every single minute, but it’s there most days, this sort of heaviness. At first I thought it was just the fallout from everything that’s been going on at school and at home, but it doesn’t seem to lift the way I expected.

Nights are the worst. I wake up from these really vivid, upsetting dreams about school shootings, angry parents, or losing my own kids in the building. I jolt awake, heart racing, and then I’m afraid to fall back asleep because it’ll just start again. I’m tired all the time.

It’s also getting harder to stay focused. In staff meetings my mind drifts, I lose track of conversations with teachers, and I find myself rereading the same email three times. It’s embarrassing in my position.

I do have thoughts like, “What’s the point?” or “It would be easier if I just didn’t wake up,” but I haven’t made any plans or anything like that. Still, it scares me that those thoughts even cross my mind. It’s definitely made it harder to do my job and be present with my family.

D013-D020_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for… I guess a bit over a year now. It’s hard to remember exactly when it started. I just know that what used to feel peaceful in the shop—the colors, the smell of the flowers—now mostly feels flat, like it’s all happening behind a pane of glass.

I’m sleeping a lot more than I used to. I’ll go to bed early, hit snooze over and over, and on my days off I can stay in bed half the morning. Even when I’m awake, I feel heavy and slow. My husband will be talking to me and I realize I’ve completely drifted off mid-conversation. I lose my place doing simple things, like writing out cards for bouquets or checking invoices. I reread the same line three times and it still doesn’t stick.

There have been moments—especially walking over the bridge to the market or crossing busy streets to pick up supplies—where this sudden urge pops up, like, “What if I just stepped off?” or “What if I just walked into the road?” I don’t plan anything, but the thought hits hard and scares me.

Some of this seemed to get worse when we had a lot of financial and family stuff going on, but I can’t tell anymore what’s just stress and what’s… something else. It’s starting to affect how I manage the business and how present I am at home.

    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D013-D020_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling for a little over a year now… maybe a year and a few months. It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. I remember crying in the conservation lab over something minor, and since then it’s like the tears are always close to the surface. I’ll be in a meeting about a new exhibition, someone makes a simple comment, and I feel my eyes fill up for no clear reason. I avoid the staff lounge because I don’t want anyone to see me like that.

I also sleep a lot more than I used to. I used to get up early to walk before work; now I can sleep ten, eleven hours and still feel like I could go back to bed. On weekends I stay in bed most of the morning, just drifting in and out.

Making basic choices has become weirdly difficult. I’ll stand in front of my closet stuck on what to wear, or stare at takeaway menus and give up because I can’t decide. It’s like everything feels heavier than it should.

With all the pressure at work and some personal stuff, I’ve had thoughts about just not being here anymore. I’ve even pictured specific ways and places I might do it, gone over the details in my head. I haven’t acted on any of it, but the thoughts come back, especially when I’m alone at home after the museum closes and the day’s stress hits me.
